Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

impressive adjective

also impressively, remarkable, striking

classical

Cic. de Or. 1.2: admīrābilis in dīcendō vir (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Lig. 6

admīrābilis, admīrābile

admirable, impressive

Worthy of admiration, of people, qualities and deeds. It also means “astonishing, strange” (Cicero’s word for the Stoic paradoxes), and it is often ironic: ō admīrābilem impudentiam! (Cic. Phil. 3.18).

Other words

  • magnificus, magnifica, magnificum — splendid, grand, impressive (of buildings, shows, preparations)

    also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 2.2: magnificae vīllae (Lewis & Short); Cic. Off. 1.25: apparātus (Lewis & Short)

    Of things, splendid and costly; of people, high-minded or fond of display, and in Plautus boastful (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • ō clēmentiam admīrābilem!

    what admirable mercy!Cic. Lig. 6 (Lewis & Short)

  • Quam magnifica vīlla!

    What an impressive house!composed
